subject: Art & Design
title: Cézanne: The Father of Modern Art
description: Learn Cézanne: The Father of Modern Art in one minute.

hook.text: Picasso called Cézanne 'the father of us all.' What did a landscape painter do to earn that?

buildup.text: Cézanne painted the same mountain — Mont Sainte-Victoire — over 80 times from different angles.

discovery.text: He broke objects into geometric planes. He showed multiple viewpoints in a single painting.

twist.text: Critics mocked his 'clumsy' drawing. He was deliberately distorting form to reveal structure.

climax.text: His geometric approach directly inspired Cubism, which shattered visual art wide open.

punchline.text: Cézanne didn't paint what he saw. He painted how seeing works.

quiz.question: Why is Cézanne called 'the father of modern art'?
options: His geometric approach to form directly inspired Cubism
He was the first to use oil paint

details.summary: Paul Cézanne (1839-1906) sought to paint nature's underlying geometric structure — cylinders, spheres, and cones beneath surface appearances. His flattened perspectives and faceted brushwork broke three-dimensional illusion, directly inspiring Picasso and Braque to develop Cubism.
details.whyItMatters: Cézanne bridged Impressionism and modern art. His obsession with structure over surface appearance gave permission for the radical experiments of Cubism, abstraction, and everything that followed in 20th-century art.
takeaways: Flattened perspective and faceted brushwork broke 3D illusion
Directly inspired Picasso and Braque to develop Cubism

faq.question: What did Cézanne mean by painting with cylinders and spheres?
faq.answer: He believed visible reality could be reduced to basic geometric forms — every tree trunk a cylinder, every apple a sphere, every mountain a cone. By painting these underlying structures rather than surface appearances, he sought a deeper truth about how we perceive the physical world.

faq.question: Why is Cézanne called the father of modern art?
faq.answer: His multiple simultaneous viewpoints and structural analysis of form directly inspired Cubism. His flattening of pictorial space anticipated abstract art. Matisse, Picasso, and Braque all acknowledged Cézanne as the artist who made their breakthroughs possible.
